q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a voltage stabilizer?
title: Voltage stabilizer carbon footprint per unit
short: A stabilizer is mostly its transformer: weigh the copper or aluminium winding and lamination steel per unit and multiply by supplier figures. Add the board, relays and cabinet, then winding, assembly and testing energy, divided by units passed.

ul: Control board, relays and a metal or plastic cabinet.
Testing across the input voltage range.

p: Report per unit by kVA rating and winding metal, since copper and aluminium windings differ in weight and footprint.

example.title: Worked example: voltage stabilizer unit per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 14,200 / 8,000 = 1.775 kg CO2 per unit
Add winding metal, steel and cabinet for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
